**NTRT gap brief — Thursday, 05 November 2026**

**Mode B — screener fallback.** TradingView public scanner; the ntrt backend was unreachable (`GET /health` → HTTP 000). Pre-market tape snapshot pulled 10:12 ET, 72 min after the 09:30 open.

**TL;DR**

- **The tape is a rotation, not a general risk-off:** 481 US stocks printed a >=3% pre-market gap; 69 cleared the actionable gate (|gap| >=3% AND >=5% of 30-day ADV) —
- 40 down, 29 up.
- **The %ADV reality check:** of the 481 gap names, only 69 cleared 5% of 30-day ADV and just 8 cleared 20%;
- 232 are quotes on essentially no volume (below 1% of ADV). The screen is much smaller than 481 tradeable names.
- **The most consequential name is MNTN -50.8% on 88% of ADV** — a Q3 miss, a 10% guidance cut and a CEO change in one print.
- The most consequential *theme* is the post-midterm rotation out of AI/data-center suppliers and into hyperscalers, clean energy and China value.

**Market backdrop**

- **The catalyst is political.** Democrats swept both chambers and the Texas governorship on 3 Nov;
- voters rejected AI data centres in 40 of 41 local ballot measures, and UBS put ~30% of expected 2028 data-centre additions at risk of delay.
- Chip and data-centre suppliers sell off; hyperscalers and clean energy bid.
- **Asia is already rotated.** Hang Seng +3.67% to 24,797 (fifth straight gain, HSTech +5.6%); Shanghai Composite +2.27%. Capital went into Chinese internet value, out of Korea/Taiwan hardware.
- **Crude and gold bid, dollar flat.** WTI $89.70 (+1.79%) after an ~8-9% plunge Wednesday on hopes of a US-Iran deal; gold $4,118.80 (+1.12%); DXY 101.61; 10y yield 4.876% (-1.8bp).
- **Live US tape at 10:10 ET (bridge, post-open):** SPY 751.48 (-2.00%), QQQ 663.28 (-4.14%), IWM 279.59 (-1.56%), TLT +0.16%, GLD +1.27%. Jobless claims printed 189k, under forecast.
- **Next week's mega-cap earnings (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft) are the next AI-capex referendum**; Nvidia reports 17 Nov.

**Worth your attention**

- Actionable set: 69 names (|gap| >=3% AND >=5% of 30-day ADV), sorted by absolute gap within each direction.
- Pre-market volume is the pre-open session only; %ADV uses TradingView's 30-session average daily volume, so 100% means the pre-market traded a full day's average.

**Flags**

- **JAN -3.4% on 92.4% of ADV is an offering, not a market view.** Janus Living priced an upsized 26.25M-share deal at $28.50 (~13.6% of shares outstanding) on 4 Nov.
- **HLP +3.1% on 101.4% of ADV is a print, not a gap** —
- Hongli Group traded more shares pre-market than it does in a normal day, on a $236K 30-day average. Treat the percentage as meaningless.
- **MNTN -50.8% on 88.1% of ADV** is the one gap-down with a genuinely heavy book; it is also the day's largest mover.
- Every other sub-20% gap in this brief traded a fraction of a normal day.
- **RZLV -3.7% on 5.2% of ADV is a continuation, not an event** — a new 52-week low ($1.37) after the H1 print, with the target cut to $5 from $12.
- No company news today.
- **IREN -4.6% is pre-print, not post-print.** IREN reports Q1 FY27 after today's close;
- the gap reflects the post-midterm neocloud de-rating (Bernstein cut its target to $55 from $100), not a result.
- **FLNC -4.3% has no new event today.** The move continues the Oct 30 CEO/CFO exits and the Sept 16 guidance cut, with securities class-action filings still arriving.
- **Four names fell despite beating:** MTSI (+63% revenue), NVMI (record Q3), COHR (beat and raised) and AMD (beat and guided above).
- A good print did not save them from the sector unwind.
- **The tape moved after the pre-open.** These are the pre-open prints;
- the regular session is already running (QQQ -4.1% at 10:10 ET), so several of these gaps have been partly or wholly retraced.
- The tables show the pre-market screen only and are not updated for the live session.
- **One catalyst could not be confirmed: TE -4.0%.** The screen carries the ticker 'TE' (NYSE, Producer Manufacturing);
- a targeted news search found no company event matching the move, so the Why cell is left unconfirmed rather than filled with a guess.

**Method, source health & caveats**

- **Primary screen — TradingView public screener, HTTP 200.** Two pulls against `POST https://scanner.tradingview.com/america/scan`: `premarket_change` in [3,1000] sorted desc (160 names) and [-1000,-3] sorted asc (321 names).
- Filters held: `type=stock` (REITs included, not re-filtered), `exchange` not OTC, `market_cap_basic` >= $200,000,000. 481 unique names at >=3% gap.
- **ntrt backend — failed.** `GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/health` → HTTP 000 (connection refused), so this is Mode B (screener fallback). No MCP mode was attempted.
- **Bridge `market-recap` —
- ok, 2 calls.** `market_snapshot` and `get_quotes` returned HTTP 200 for the market backdrop and for previous-close verification only (SPY 766.81, QQQ 691.95, and APP's 271.75 Nov-4 close all matched the screener-derived values exactly).
- **MCP probe — `catalog_ok total=135 finance_tools=0`**, bridge reachable with packs tradier, fmp, market-recap. No finance MCP is registered on this runtime, so the public screener was used, per the skill.
- **Catalysts — `web_search`** for all 69 actionable names, cross-checked against company releases (Business Wire / GlobeNewswire / StockTitan), AP, Reuters and investing.com.
- One catalyst could not be confirmed (TE) and is flagged rather than filled in.
- **Previous close is derived, not quoted.** TradingView's `close` column is the LIVE intraday price once the session is open (SPY `close` 754.64 vs the Nov-4 close 766.81), so it cannot be used as the prior close.
- Prior close was derived as `premarket_close / (1 + premarket_change)` and validated against the bridge for three names — exact match on all three.
- **Yahoo pre-market was not used for any published price.** Yahoo reports 0 volume on every pre-market bar and its tape goes stale on thin names;
- pre-market volume here is TradingView's own `premarket_volume`.
- **Denominator caveat:** `average_volume_30d_calc` is a 30-session DAILY average, so a %ADV above 100 means the pre-open session alone traded more than a normal full day.
- Two names (JAN, HLP) are affected.
- **One pull, one screen.** Every number in this brief and in the CSV comes from the single pre-market pull pair above;
- the market backdrop quotes the bridge's 15:10Z snapshot and is labelled with its time. Names whose gap crossed the 3% threshold after the pull would not appear here.
